newsitem.title: UK: Windfall tax may threaten UK utilites' ratings-S&P.
newsitem.headline: Windfall tax may threaten UK utilites' ratings-S&P.

text.p: U.S. credit rating agency Standard & Poor's said on Friday it may cut the ratings of many British utilities following details of how the new Labour government will levy its one-off windfall tax on their profits.

Chancellor of the Exchequer (Finance Minister) Gordon Brown announced in his budget speech on Wednesday that the tax would raise around 2.1 billion pounds ($3.5 billion) from the electricity sector, some 1.65 billion from water companies and another 1.45 billion from other privatised utilities.

"The announcement of the formula for the windfall tax removes an element of uncertainty from the utility sector," Standard & Poor's said in a statement. "However, the relative size of the imposition on the water and electricity distribution sector is greater than anticipated."
Credit ratings affect the interest rate at which a company can borrow funds and are closely watched by industry analysts.

S&P said Anglian Water Plc, Hyder Plc, Northumbrian Water Group, Thames Water Plc, Yorkshire Water Plc, and United Utilities Plc had all been placed on CreditWatch with negative implications. It added the short term ratings of Hyder, Northumbrian Water and Thames Water would remain unchanged.
S&P said while the imposition of the windfall tax would lead to weaker financial profiles on all utilities affected, the precise impact on each utility would depend on how the tax was financed.
"This could involve a combination of new debt, equity infusions, lower dividends, use of reserves, and further capital and operating expenditure reductions," S&P said.

S&P said it would review the situation as soon as possible. "Standard & Poor's believes that should some of the ratings be lowered, it would be unlikely to be by more than one rating notch," the agency said.
It said British Telecommunications Plc would remain on CreditWatch with negative implications, where it was placed following the announcement of the merger with MCI.
S&P said the credit ratings of PowerGen Plc, National Power, Railtrack Plc and BAA Plc were among those that would be unaffected by the windfall tax. ($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
